title: The guard on the guard can be switched off or fooled

candidates.pattern: Gate-conformance test: a test that reads the gate's OWN configuration (build file, hook, compiler flags), strips comments first, and fails on the known ways of switching the gate off or downgrading it — so disarming a gate is itself a red test, not a later discovery.
candidates.failurePrevented: A pre-commit hook with TEST_CMD emptied (the hook's own contract: `[ -z "$2" ] && return 0` skips silently), `npm run chaos` added to pre-commit (it rewrites shipped source), tsconfig `strict`/`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` flipped, eslint dropping strictTypeChecked, or vitest `include` narrowed — each of which leaves every existing test green while the gate checks less.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:15-23 "nothing in the suite would notice the gate being switched off, downgraded to a warning, or left behind by a new subpackage. These assertions read {@code build.gradle.kts} and the {@code package-info.java} files directly"; :34-36 SILENT_SWITCH_OFFS = enabled.set(false), disable("NullAway"), excludedPaths, errorproneArgs, -XepDisableAllChecks ...; :66-68 "NullAway must fail the app/ compile, not warn — a warning nobody reads is not a gate". Commit 88b142ee: "Both gate conformance tests matched raw substrings of build.gradle.kts, so enabled.set(false), disable(\"NullAway\"), an excludedPaths option, or a required line moved into a comment all passed. They now strip comments first, assert the ERROR line inside the compileJava block rather than anywhere in the file, and fail on each of the known switch-offs."
candidates.builtAndExercised: BUILT and hardened once already: 88b142ee (2026-09-06) closed the comment/substring false-pass; NullnessGateConformanceTest.java and ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest.java exist; AGENTS.md:508-510 "NullnessGateConformanceTest fails if a package inside the scope has no @NullMarked package-info, if the checker is downgraded below ERROR, or if models reappears in the list."
candidates.ourEvidence: Searched SSHD tests/ and scripts/ for hooksPath|pre-commit|eslint.config|strictTypeChecked|githooks: hits only in tests/chaosGate.test.ts (reads chaos.ts EXPECTED_TOTAL — a partial instance of the pattern), tests/game-purity-ratchet.test.ts (a `.tick(` source scan), tests/claimcheck.test.ts (prose). Nothing reads .githooks/pre-commit, tsconfig.json, eslint.config.mjs or vite.config.ts. .githooks/pre-commit:5 "Leave one \"\" to skip that step" and :31 `[ -z "$2" ] && return 0` — the skip is by design and unguarded. agent-harness commit-gate/ ships the template with no conformance test. Memory reference-global-ship-bar-hook: "live hook is UNGUARDED (measured 2026-09-14); new-project.sh ... wrote invalid JSON" — a gate config that was silently broken is a failure this account has already had.
candidates.proposal: SSHD tests/gate-conformance.test.ts (~40 lines, node:fs only): strip `#`/`//`/`/* */` comments, then assert (a) .githooks/pre-commit sets BUILD_CMD="npm run -s typecheck", TEST_CMD="npx vitest run", LINT_CMD="npm run -s lint" (non-empty, exact) and contains no `chaos` token; (b) tsconfig.json parses with strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride true; (c) eslint.config.mjs contains `strictTypeChecked` and `stylisticTypeChecked`; (d) vite.config.ts include is 'tests/**/*.test.ts'. Register two plants in a tests/gates.plants.ts (file field is ROOT-relative, so `.githooks/pre-commit` and `tsconfig.json` are plantable) — matches the harness's existing plant shape. Second target, later and separately: a harness-side check that ~/.claude/settings.json parses and its ship-bar hook command resolves.
candidates.doneCriterion: npm run chaos: plant TEST_CMD="" in .githooks/pre-commit → the named test goes RED (a failed test, not a compile error); plant "strict": false in tsconfig.json → RED; both restore byte-identical; chaos plant count rises 43 → 45 and tests/chaosGate.test.ts + scripts/gates/chaos.ts EXPECTED_TOTAL move together.
candidates.cost: ~40 lines test + ~20 lines plants; zero dependencies; ~5 ms per run.
candidates.why: It closes a whole class (gate quietly disarmed) for the price of one small test, and the account already paid for this lesson on the ship-bar hook. Adapt, not adopt: our gates are shell/JSON/TS config, not a Gradle DSL, and comment-stripping plus exact-command equality is enough — no block-scoping needed.

candidates.pattern: Fail the suite on a focused test (`it.only` / `describe.only`) in every environment, not only under CI
candidates.failurePrevented: A session debugs with `it.only`, forgets it, commits: vitest runs ONE test in that file, reports the rest as skipped, exits 0, and the pre-commit gate passes. Because the hook also exits 0 whenever `$CI` is set, there is no environment on this machine where vitest's own CI guard would ever fire.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:13 "Guards the one way this suite can lie: silently running nothing (JCLAW-1176)." — same family (a suite that reports green over tests it never ran). JClaw's runner cannot express `.only`; the lesson transfers as the vitest-specific switch.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commit 5cd087a1 2026-09-10 "test(discovery): fail the build on a test class the runner never reaches (JCLAW-1176)"; header line 18 names the real victim: "MultiImageVideoAdapterTest sat that way with two live test methods until this check found it". OUR side MEASURED in the scratchpad with SSHD's own vitest 4.1.10: default run of a file with `it.only` → `Tests 1 passed | 1 skipped (2)`, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`; with `--allowOnly=false` → `FAIL t/a.test.mjs > focused  Error: [Vitest] Unexpected .only modifier`.
candidates.ourEvidence: vite.config.ts is 8 lines: `test: { include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts'], environment: 'node' }` — no `allowOnly`. `grep -rn 'allowOnly\|passWithNoTests\|no-focused-tests\|eslint-plugin-vitest' vite.config.ts eslint.config.mjs package.json tests` → empty. `grep -rnE '\b(it|test|describe)\.(only)\(' tests --include='*.ts'` → 0 hits today (so nothing is broken now; nothing would catch it tomorrow). Context7 /vitest-dev/vitest defaults.ts: `allowOnly: !isCI`. .githooks/pre-commit:12 `[ -n "$CI" ] && exit 0` — the hook never runs under CI, so vitest's CI guard is unreachable here.
candidates.proposal: vite.config.ts, one line inside `test: {}`: `allowOnly: false, // a forgotten it.only shrinks a file to one test and the gate stays green (measured 2026-09-14)`. Optionally one chaos plant in tests/*.plants.ts that inserts `.only` into a test and names that file — but the plant harness requires a FAILED test, which this produces, so it fits.
candidates.doneCriterion: Add `it.only` to any test in tests/, run `npx vitest run` → exit non-zero with `Unexpected .only modifier`; remove it → green with the same total as before (RESUME_HERE: 1631).
candidates.cost: 1 line; 0 tokens per turn; 0 dependencies; ~2 min.
candidates.why: Smallest possible change that closes a measured fail-open; nothing else in the toolchain (no vitest eslint plugin, no CI) can see it.

candidates.pattern: Every file that declares tests must be one the runner collects — compare the runner's discovery against the tree, with a floor so an empty scan cannot pass
candidates.failurePrevented: A session writes `tests/npcSlice4.spec.ts` or `src/core/x.test.ts` (both are vitest's DEFAULT spellings; many skills/templates use `.spec.ts`). Our include is the narrower `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so the file compiles, is linted, and never runs; the suite is green. vitest's `passWithNoTests: false` only covers the case where ZERO files match.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/TestDiscoveryConformanceTest.java:15-19 "A plain JUnit class under test/ compiles, is never executed, and the suite still reports green — so the failure mode is an absence, which no assertion inside that class can ever report."; :64 `assertTrue(examined > 400, "the scan reached only " + examined + " files — it is not measuring the suite")`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commit 5cd087a1 2026-09-10; AGENTS.md:31 "A class that extends neither play.test.UnitTest nor FunctionalTest never runs; TestDiscoveryConformanceTest now fails the build on one, so it no longer needs watching by hand." The predicate has its own shape test (`thePredicateNamesTheShapeItIsLookingFor`).
candidates.ourEvidence: `find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o \( -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.spec.ts' -o -name '*.test.mts' -o -name '*.test.js' \) -print | grep -v '^./tests/'` → nothing (no orphan today). tests/chaosGate.test.ts:118-125 already shells `npx vitest list --filesOnly` but only asserts `.plants.ts` is NOT in it — the inverse direction (everything that should be collected IS) is nowhere. tests/utils/npcHarness.ts:36 relies on the narrow include by comment only: "NOT collected as a suite: vite.config.ts sets include: ['tests/**\/*.test.ts']".
candidates.proposal: tests/chaosGate.test.ts (it already has the `vitest list --filesOnly` call and the ROOT): one more `it`: build `declared` = every `git ls-files` path under tests/ or src/ whose text matches `/^\s*(describe|it|test)(\.each)?\(/m` and is not in tests/utils/ or tests/fixtures/; assert `declared ⊆ collected` and `collected.length >= 80` (83 files today) so a parser that matches nothing cannot pass.
candidates.doneCriterion: Create tests/probe.spec.ts containing one `it(...)` → the new test fails naming `tests/probe.spec.ts`; rename to `.test.ts` → passes. The floor: temporarily set the include glob to `tests/zz/**` → the test fails on the floor, not vacuously.
candidates.cost: ~12 lines in an existing file; ~1 s added to the suite (one more `vitest list` — reuse the existing call's output); 0 per-turn tokens.
candidates.why: Exact JClaw shape, but reuse the discovery call chaosGate already makes rather than a new file; the narrow include is a deliberate choice (keeps plants and helpers out) so guard it instead of widening it.

candidates.pattern: Gate-wiring conformance: a test that reads the hook and the checker configs with comments stripped and asserts the gate is wired, on, and at error severity — including that git is actually pointed at the hook
candidates.failurePrevented: Three silent switch-offs: (a) a fresh clone or a new machine has no `core.hooksPath`, so `.githooks/pre-commit` never fires and every commit is ungated (JClaw: "hooks silently don't fire"); (b) one of the hook's three commands set to `""` (the file itself advertises `Leave one "" to skip that step`), so a step is disabled with the tick still printed for the others; (c) a checker downgraded — `allowOnly` re-added as true, `strict` flipped, `strictTypeChecked` swapped for `recommended`, the eslint `ignores` list widened — with no test noticing.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/NullnessGateConformanceTest.java:20-22 "These assertions read build.gradle.kts and the package-info.java files directly, which is the only way to make those three regressions fail a test run rather than a later push."; :67-68 `check("NullAway", CheckSeverity.ERROR)` "a warning nobody reads is not a gate"; test/ResourceLeakGateConformanceTest.java:50-53 `withoutComments` "Comments are where a required token survives after the code that needed it is gone."; AGENTS.md:85 "Without the setup, hooks silently don't fire and /deploy fails on the github push."
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: commits b87f4384 / 19d873dc 2026-09-05/06 (gates added with their conformance tests in the same change) and 88b142ee 2026-09-06 (the switch-off deny-list added after the first version was found blind). hooksPath is handled by `./jclaw.sh setup` (AGENTS.md:80-85), a setup step, not a test.
candidates.ourEvidence: `git config core.hooksPath` in SSHD → `.githooks` (wired on THIS machine only); `grep -rn hooksPath CLAUDE.md RESUME_HERE.md docs/research/HARNESS.md src/*/CLAUDE.md` → nothing; `grep -rnE 'pre-commit|hooksPath|tsconfig|eslint\.config|vite\.config|package\.json' tests scripts --include='*.ts'` → only comments (chaosGate.test.ts:4, claimcheck.test.ts:2,12, npcHarness.ts:36) — no test reads any of these files. .githooks/pre-commit:3 "Leave one "" to skip that step." Per-line switch-offs are not a live problem: `grep -rnE 'eslint-disable|@ts-ignore|@ts-expect-error|@ts-nocheck' src tests scripts --include='*.ts'` → 1 hit, with a reason (tests/progression.test.ts:219).
candidates.proposal: tests/gateWiring.test.ts, ~30 lines, four `it`s, each reading the file via a tiny `withoutComments` (strip `/*…*/`, `//…`, `#…` for sh): (1) `execFileSync('git',['config','core.hooksPath'])` trims to `.githooks` and `.githooks/pre-commit` is executable (`statSync(...).mode & 0o111`); (2) the hook's `BUILD_CMD=`, `TEST_CMD=`, `LINT_CMD=` are each non-empty and TEST_CMD contains `vitest run`; (3) vite.config.ts contains `allowOnly: false` and `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`; (4) tsconfig.json has `"strict": true` and eslint.config.mjs contains `strictTypeChecked` and its `ignores` array equals the four entries it has today. Assert positives with comments stripped; skip JClaw's negative string blacklist (see antiPattern 2).
candidates.doneCriterion: `git config --unset core.hooksPath && npx vitest run tests/gateWiring.test.ts` → red naming hooksPath; `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` → green. Set `LINT_CMD=""` in the hook → red; restore → green. All four assertions watched red once by hand before commit (ship-bar rule 3).
candidates.cost: ~30 lines, one new test file, +4 tests, <50 ms; 0 per-turn tokens; ~25 min including the red-first pass.
candidates.why: Insurance, not a bleeding wound (the tree has one annotated `@ts-expect-error` and no `.only`), but each assertion is a line, the hooksPath one turns 'a fresh clone has no gate' from silent to red, and it is the natural home for gate-guards-1's `allowOnly: false` so a later 'tidy' cannot remove it. Keep it to the four assertions above — a longer token list is churn.

candidates.pattern: Two copies of one gate rule are pinned equal or collapsed to one — schema/enum drift between the thing that documents and the thing that enforces fails a test
candidates.failurePrevented: SSHD's scripts/gates/chaosLib.ts and agent-harness's harness/chaos/chaosLib.mjs implement the same verdict rules (testCounts / classify / baselineIsGreen); the public copy was hardened past the SSHD copy by an adversarial review, so today the two disagree on real inputs (signals, locks, unknown flags, tree-wide drift). That is the 'state-schema drift' killer, self-inflicted, in the gate that certifies the other gates.
candidates.jclawEvidence: test/EvalSuiteConformanceTest.java:53-65 `schemaAndLoaderAgreeOnTheCheckVocabulary` — "Drift between them ships a documented kind that no run can use" / `assertEquals(implemented, documented)`; test/ApiConversationsControllerSchemaDriftTest.java:23-30 "hand-maintained beside HashMap-based emitters ... so a new map key can silently drift out of the OpenAPI contract".
candidates.builtAndExercised: JClaw: EvalSuite test in commit a486bb37 2026-07-27 (JCLAW-875); schema-drift test in fba91690 2026-07-22 (JCLAW-815); both run on every `play autotest`.
candidates.ourEvidence: HAVE the cross-read for one value: tests/chaosGate.test.ts:70-75 reads `/const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);/` out of scripts/gates/chaos.ts and asserts it equals its own 43 ("One rule, one number: read the runner's constant rather than trusting a copy"). HAVE for workflows: tests/workflowScripts.test.ts:114-139 pins measure-verify's dead-branch vocabulary; measure-refute.js:96 `LIVE = new Set(['CLEAN','CORRECTED','FATAL'])` matches measure-verify.js:116's enum minus UNVERIFIED. GAP for the chaos lib: RESUME_HERE.md:83-88 "⚠️ This repo's chaos runner shares holes the agent-harness port closed ... Port the rest from ~/kheshav-code/agent-harness/harness/chaos/chaos.mjs in the next harness session."; HARNESS.md:257-259 "hardened past this copy by an adversarial review". No test compares the two libs.
candidates.proposal: Delete over add: replace scripts/gates/chaos.ts + chaosLib.ts with the vendored harness/chaos/chaos.mjs + chaosLib.mjs (zero-dep files, not a dependency — SSHD's 'no new runtime dependency' rule is intact) and a `chaos.config.json` (`plantsDir: tests`, `expectedTotal: 43`, `testCommand: ['npx','vitest','run']`, `summary: 'vitest'`); keep tests/chaosGate.test.ts importing from the .mjs (it already runs `--check`-equivalent logic) and drop its private copy of the count in favour of reading chaos.config.json. If the port is deferred again: a 10-line pin in chaosGate.test.ts that feeds the same 6 summary-line fixtures (already at :128-206) to BOTH libs and asserts identical verdicts.
candidates.doneCriterion: `npm run chaos` → 43/43 RED using the vendored runner; `git grep -n 'function classify' scripts/` → exactly one definition; the harness's own plants still 33/33 RED in agent-harness (its copy is the canonical one).
candidates.cost: One harness session (already scheduled in RESUME_HERE); or 10 lines for the pin. Removes ~500 lines net.
candidates.why: Already owed and self-diagnosed; JClaw's contribution is the pin shape for the interim. The full replacement is the simplest END state; the pin is the simplest NEXT step.

candidates.pattern: A gate that reads a config or source file by raw substring passes when the line it guards is commented out
candidates.failurePrevented: The guard on a guard silently stops guarding: the value it reads comes from a comment, so the live value can be anything.
candidates.jclawEvidence: Commit 88b142ee 2026-09-06 `test(gates): close the silent switch-offs the conformance tests could not see`: `Both gate conformance tests matched raw substrings of build.gradle.kts, so enabled.set(false), disable("NullAway"), an excludedPaths option, or a required line moved into a comment all passed. They now strip comments first, assert the ERROR line inside the compileJava block rather than anywhere in the file, and fail on each of the known switch-offs.` Same commit: `The Lucene scan accepted a release anywhere in the file, including at the end of a test body where a failing assertion skips it`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Yes — the fix ships the negative cases as assertions ('fail on each of the known switch-offs'), i.e. the gate's own false-pass modes became tests.
candidates.ourEvidence: LIVE SITE: tests/chaosGate.test.ts:73 `const found = /const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);/.exec(src)?.[1];` — no `^` anchor, no `m` flag, and `.exec` takes the FIRST match. scripts/gates/chaos.ts:81 is `const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;`. A stale commented copy left above it (`// const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;`) while the live line became a computed expression would satisfy the regex from the comment and the test would pass while the runner's real number came from somewhere else — defeating the test's own stated purpose, the comment at :70 `One rule, one number: read the runner's constant rather than trusting a copy.` The opposite direction is already safe: rename or delete the constant and `.exec` returns null, so `expect(undefined).toBe('43')` fails closed (reasoned from the code, not executed). Our other source-reading gates are stronger: claimcheck parses rather than substring-matches, and tests/configTwins.test.ts pins 36 with a deny-list.
candidates.proposal: Anchor the regex to a line start with no leading comment marker and assert exactly one match: `/^const EXPECTED_TOTAL = (\d+);$/m` plus a check that the file contains no second occurrence of the identifier in an assignment position.
candidates.doneCriterion: Insert `// const EXPECTED_TOTAL = 43;` above scripts/gates/chaos.ts:81 and change the live line to a computed value → the test goes RED; restore → GREEN with 1631 tests unchanged.
candidates.cost: ~3 lines in one existing test; 0 runtime cost.
candidates.why: The one candidate in this unit with a live false-pass site in our own gate-guard, and the fix is three lines in a test that already exists.

candidates.pattern: Detect that the hook path is not wired, and say so
candidates.failurePrevented: A fresh clone or a new worktree has `core.hooksPath` unset, so every gate is silently absent and every commit is ungated.
candidates.jclawEvidence: jclaw.sh:1295-1299 `hooks_path=$(/usr/bin/git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" config --local core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null || true)` / `if [[ "$hooks_path" != ".githooks" ]]; then` / `echo "...Setup hasn't run on this clone yet. Run ${INVOKE} setup..."`, and jclaw.sh:2472 `/usr/bin/git config --local core.hooksPath .githooks` in setup. A post-checkout hook (.githooks/post-checkout:39-40) re-runs init-worktree on `git worktree add`.
candidates.builtAndExercised: Built and live, but as a HINT in the CLI's help footer, not a gate — the comment at jclaw.sh:1288-1292 calls it a 'First-run hint footer'. Nothing fails. Honest reading: JClaw does not solve this either; it nudges.
candidates.ourEvidence: `git config --get core.hooksPath` → `.githooks` on this clone, so we are wired today. `grep -rn hooksPath tests/ scripts/ package.json` → empty: nothing asserts it, and .githooks/ holds only pre-commit (no post-checkout).
candidates.proposal: A one-line assertion in an existing test that `core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`.
candidates.doneCriterion: `git config --unset core.hooksPath` → the test goes RED; restore → GREEN.
candidates.cost: ~5 lines, one `git config` exec per suite run.
candidates.why: Cheap and real — but the honest weakness is that the test only runs if a gate runs, and the failure it guards is 'no gate runs'. It catches the case where the suite is invoked by hand or by CI, not the fresh-clone case, and the proposal must say so rather than overclaim.
